title: Your first Dockerfile
idea: A Dockerfile is a recipe: each line adds a layer to an image, and Docker reuses every layer that has not changed.

analogy.text: Baking a layer cake. Change the top layer and you only rebake the top; change the bottom and you start over.
analogy.breaks: Layers stack in the order you write them; order is the whole trick.

points: `FROM` picks the base image your app builds on.
`COPY` and `RUN` each create a new cached layer.
Copy `package.json` first, install, then copy the rest, so installs stay cached.
`CMD` is the command that runs when the container starts.

hero.title: Order decides the cache

left.title: Slow: copy everything first
items: Any code edit invalidates the install layer

right.title: Fast: dependencies first
items: COPY package*.json, then RUN npm ci
Code edits only rebuild the last layers
Installs come from cache in seconds

hero.verdict: Order lines from least to most often changed.

code.caption: A production-minded Dockerfile for a Node 20 app. Step through it line by line.

walk.text: Start from a small official Node 20 image. Alpine keeps it light.
Work inside /app so paths stay short and predictable.
Copy only the package files first. This layer rarely changes.
Install production dependencies. Cached until the package files change.
Now copy your source. Edits here no longer trigger a reinstall.
Document the port. It does not publish it; the -p flag does.
Set the start command that every container runs.

pitfalls: Copying `node_modules` from your laptop bloats the image; add a `.dockerignore`.
Apple Silicon builds arm64 images; add `--platform linux/amd64` for most servers.
Run as a non-root user in production: add `USER node`.

quiz.q: You edit only server.js. Which layers rebuild?
quiz.why: Layers above the changed COPY come from cache. That line and the ones after it rebuild.

takeaway: Put what changes least at the top, so Docker can reuse its cache.

starters: What is the difference between an image and a container?
